items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: So really that feeling of what we’re playing is kind of loosely, in my humble ability, to try to come from that spirit or the energy that John Coltrane played from.

ctx.x: Yeah. Probably got surrounded there. Just to go back to the composing for a bit, you have a tune that you wrote called “Mr. Jones” I believe. And was there a reason that you chose, I think it’s either 6/8 or 3/4 groove. Is there a reason for that?

Well I love Elvin’s playing on 3/4. If you listen to him on recordings with John, there’s one that they do called “Spiritual,” which is in C minor. So really that feeling of what we’re playing is kind of loosely, in my humble ability, to try to come from that spirit or the energy that John Coltrane played from. “Live at the Vanguard” is our spiritual, is our spirit, which as a group is from that. So it is my appreciation for Elvin’s ability to play in 3/4.
Okay. And there was one more I wanted to ask you about, “Mr. Taylor.”
